task.title: Creating service keys for standalone Red Hat Quay
task.shortdesc: To create service keys for standalone Red Hat Quay read-only mode, you can generate a key pair inside the Quay container or in a local Python virtual environment.

ul.li:
If you are using Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) 7.x:
You have enabled the Red Hat Software Collections List (RHSCL).
You have installed Python 3.6.
You have downloaded the virtualenv package.
You have installed the git CLI.

If you are using Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) 8:
You have installed Python 3 on your machine.
You have downloaded the python3-virtualenv package.
You have installed the git CLI.
You have cloned the quay/quay repository from GitHub.

context.p: Red Hat Quay uses service keys to communicate with various components. These keys are used to sign completed requests, such as requesting to scan images, login, storage access, and so on.

step.cmd: If your Red Hat Quay registry is readily available, you can generate service keys inside of the Quay registry container.

substep.cmd: Enter the following command to generate a key pair inside of the Quay container:

info.codeblock: $ podman exec quay python3 tools/generatekeypair.py quay-readonly

step.cmd: If your Red Hat Quay is not readily available, you must generate your service keys inside of a virtual environment.
